issues.title: Phase 1 finding: semantic-equivalent candidates were incorrectly encoded as framing variables
issues.body:
## Found during

ECv4.4 residual-detector qualification of the new fixed S3 semantic-state artifact.

## Finding

Fixture M009 represents two semantically equivalent valid actions. The first S3 state generator encoded those two candidate actions as two framing variables with the same `semantic_key`. ECv4.4 correctly classified that state as `DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_VARIABLES`, but the duplication is artificial: candidate alternatives belong in S2, not in the problem-model variable set.

## Impact

This would make ECv4.4 appear to over-reframe when the actual error is a layer-boundary violation in the benchmark state representation.

## Repair

- Represent the shared semantic concept once in S3 framing state.
- Keep the two equivalent alternatives exclusively in S2 candidate set.
- Restrict S3 `goal_coverage` to evidence-backed/actionable framing variables rather than blindly all variables.
- Re-run residual qualification.

## AC

- M009 no longer emits `DUPLICATE_SEMANTIC_VARIABLES` from the fixed upstream framing state.
- M005 still emits `UNEXPLAINED_OBSERVATION`.
- Other fixtures remain clean at S3 unless their scenario intentionally contains a framing residual.

issues.title: Phase 1 blocker: S2 cannot distinguish competing vs semantically equivalent valid candidates
issues.body:
## Found during

Deterministic EC S3/S4 qualification on Phase 1 v2.

## Finding

M003 and M009 both generate two valid candidates using the same `semantic_transition.operation` plus only a variant number. However:

- M003 expects both competing admissible branches to remain open (`CONTINUE`).
- M009 expects two semantically equivalent outputs to be acceptable and closable (`CLOSE`).

The persisted S2 candidate artifact lacks a semantic relation that distinguishes `COMPETING_ALTERNATIVES` from `SEMANTIC_EQUIVALENTS`.

## Impact

No S4 implementation can infer the expected closure class from the fixed upstream artifact without hidden metadata. This violates controlled intervention and makes M003 vs M009 unidentifiable.

## Required repair

Add implementation-independent candidate relation metadata, e.g.:

- `relation_groups`: group id, relation type (`EQUIVALENT` / `COMPETING`), candidate ids

or an equivalent explicit semantic relation.

M003 must expose two distinct competing transitions. M009 must expose an equivalence relation between its two valid transitions.

## AC

- S4 can distinguish M003 from M009 without hidden evaluation metadata.
- M003 closes as `CONTINUE` because unresolved competing alternatives remain.
- M009 can close as `CLOSE` because selected alternatives are semantically equivalent.
- Same upstream candidate artifact is used by LLM and EC variants.

issues.title: Phase 1 measurement: fixed-candidate LLM vs EC selection/control
issues.body:
## Objective

Run the first actual controlled comparison at the coarse layer boundary most relevant to the current hypothesis:

- C: fixed S2 candidate set + lightweight LLM selection/reframing/closure
- D: the identical fixed S2 candidate set + deterministic EC selection/reframing/closure

The S3 semantic-state artifact is also held identical by hash.

## Why this is first

This isolates candidate generation from candidate selection/control. If EC materially outperforms LLM here, the difference cannot be attributed to S2 candidate coverage.

## Inputs

- Phase 1 v2 canonical candidate set
- fixed S3 semantic state
- no hidden evaluation metadata exposed to either implementation

## LLM constraint

Use a lightweight local model where possible. Cache the output once. Large LLM is not required.

## Metrics

- selection accuracy
- reframe accuracy / residual recall
- closure accuracy / false closure
- final task success
- token/latency where available

## AC

1. LLM and EC runs have identical `candidate_set_hash` and `semantic_state_hash` per fixture.
2. LLM output is cached and replayable.
3. Hidden evaluation metadata is read only by scorer.
4. EC qualification remains 10/10 before comparison.
5. The comparison result does not claim anything about S1/S2 generation quality.
6. GitHub Actions remain disabled.

issues.title: Sandbox model import RCA: binary safe-open/DNS boundary blocks GitHub/HF/PyPI direct download
issues.body:
## Issue statement
Sandbox inference is possible, but importing a ~100 MB GGUF is blocked by transport-layer constraints, not by model/runtime capacity.

## Observed paths
1. Hugging Face: model URL resolves, then redirects through Xet/AWS signed CDN; sandbox safe-open rejects the redirected binary path.
2. PyPI wheel: model-containing wheel exists, but shell-side DNS is unavailable; binary URL also hits safe-open requirements.
3. GitHub raw/release candidate: raw URL is valid, but shell-side DNS fails (`Temporary failure in name resolution`). Container downloader requires the exact URL to have been viewed first; web cannot render binary raw URL and returns cache miss.
4. Google Drive: prior model shards are incomplete / wrapper-based. One old temp SmolLM shard contained only the first ~6 MiB and was removed as unused. COGCOMP model shards remain under investigation.

## Root cause
The active blocker is the boundary between web-safe URL validation and container binary download, plus lack of outbound DNS from the shell. This is independent of model size and inference runtime.

## Evidence
- Historical sandbox run successfully imported `SmolLM2-135M-Instruct-Q4_K_M.gguf` (~101 MB) and ran llama.cpp inference.
- Current shell DNS test against `raw.githubusercontent.com` fails with `Temporary failure in name resolution`.
- Container downloader rejects raw GitHub binary URL because it was not successfully viewed by the web layer; web binary open returns cache miss.

## Required resolution
Establish one approved binary ingress path with no unviewable redirect. Candidate order:
1. connector/file-reference path that materializes bytes directly into sandbox;
2. GitHub release/raw asset if an authenticated connector can return file bytes instead of UTF-8 text;
3. Drive stored raw file / connector file reference;
4. dedicated binary relay only if connector-native paths cannot provide bytes.

## Acceptance criteria
- One real pretrained GGUF >= 90 MB is materialized in sandbox.
- SHA-256 and GGUF magic are verified.
- llama.cpp or equivalent produces a non-empty inference result.
- Import method is documented in repo.
- Unused sandbox/Drive model artifacts are deleted.

GitHub Actions must remain disabled.

issues.title: Ingress infra: version and isolate Apps Script binary-fetch namespace
issues.body:
Discovered during sandbox LLM ingress RCA on 2026-10-01.

Problem:
- Historical `COGCOMP_FETCH_PART(kind,index)` successfully staged model/runtime binaries into `Public Fetch Smoke Test Runtime`.
- The same global Apps Script function name was later shadowed/replaced by unrelated YouTube logic.
- Re-evaluating `=COGCOMP_FETCH_PART("RUNTIME",0)` now returns `YT_DIRECT_AUDIO_NOT_FOUND` instead of binary data.

Impact:
- New runtime/model part recovery cannot safely call the historical name.
- Existing literal staging data remains valid and allowed the model to be reconstructed.

Required fix / AC:
- Introduce a versioned unique function name, e.g. `LLMEC_BINARY_FETCH_PART_V1`.
- Function has no dependency on unrelated application code.
- MODEL and RUNTIME URLs, expected sizes and SHA256 are explicit constants/config.
- Each returned part includes index, byte range, byte length, SHA256 and Base64 chunks.
- A smoke test fetches one small range and verifies SHA.
- No GitHub Actions.

RCA details: `docs/RCA_SANDBOX_LLM_INGRESS_2026-10-01.md`.
